purpose: Complete curated wrong-answer coverage for every one of the 110 original first-mock eligible Maths core flashcards, and remove three accidentally accepted inadequate/garbled responses.

answers: a^, for the same non-zero base.
is a factor of the polynomial.

scope: AQA first mock Maths Year 1 Pure only; no mechanics, statistics or Year 2

records.subject: Maths
records.back: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate a−√b.
addedAccepted: Multiply top and bottom by a minus square root b, the conjugate of the denominator.
addedRejected: Multiply numerator and denominator only by (a+sqrt b).
Multiply the numerator by a-sqrt b but leave the denominator unchanged.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: How can a^x=b be rewritten using logs?
addedAccepted: For valid a and b, x=log base a of b.
addedRejected: x=log base b of a.
x=a times log b.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: What identity links sin²θ and cos²θ?
addedRejected: sin squared theta plus cos squared theta equals zero.
sin squared theta minus cos squared theta equals one.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: When solving sin x=k, why should you check beyond the calculator's principal value?
records.back: Trigonometric functions are periodic and can have multiple solutions in the specified interval.
addedAccepted: Sine is periodic, so there may be additional angle solutions within the required interval.
addedRejected: The inverse sine calculator returns all solutions in every interval.
There can only ever be one solution to sin x=k.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: Which direction does y=f(x−a) translate a graph if a>0?
addedAccepted: Translate the graph a units in the positive x direction.
addedRejected: The graph moves a units to the left.
The graph moves a units upwards.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: What does a negative discriminant say about real roots?
records.back: A quadratic with real coefficients has no real roots if b²−4ac<0.
addedAccepted: Discriminant below zero means no solutions in the real numbers.
addedRejected: A negative discriminant gives two different real roots.
A negative discriminant gives one repeated real root.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: When cancelling a common factor from an algebraic fraction, what restriction must be retained?
records.back: Any input that made the original denominator zero remains excluded.
addedAccepted: The values that zero the original denominator are still excluded even after cancellation.
addedRejected: After cancelling the common factor, all former denominator zeros are allowed.
Removing a common factor changes the original domain to include its zeros.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: State the index law a^m × a^n.
records.back: a^(m+n), for the same non-zero base.
addedAccepted: a^m multiplied by a^n equals a^(m+n), for the same base.
addedRejected: a^(mn) is the product of a^m and a^n.
a^m+a^n is the product of two powers with base a.
invalidLegacyAccepted: a^, for the same non-zero base.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: What does a remainder of zero show about a polynomial divisor (x−a)?
records.back: (x−a) is a factor of the polynomial.
addedAccepted: If f(a)=0 then (x-a) divides f(x), so (x-a) is a factor.
addedRejected: A zero remainder when dividing by (x-a) proves (x+a) must be a factor.
A zero remainder proves the polynomial has no factor (x-a).
invalidLegacyAccepted: is a factor of the polynomial.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: What are the asymptotes of y = k/x when k≠0?
addedAccepted: Its horizontal and vertical asymptotes are y=0 and x=0 respectively.
addedRejected: The asymptotes of k/x are x=k and y=k.
The only asymptote of k/x is y=k.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: State the change-of-base formula for logₐx.
records.back: logₐx = ln x / ln a (a>0, a≠1; x>0).
addedAccepted: For a>0 with a not 1 and x>0, log base a of x is ln(x)/ln(a).
addedRejected: log_a x = ln(a)/ln(x).
log_a x = ln(a*x).

records.subject: Maths
records.front: On division of polynomial f(x) by (x−a), what is the remainder?
addedAccepted: The remainder from division of f(x) by (x-a) is its value at a.
addedRejected: The remainder is the derivative f'(a).
The remainder is f(-a) for divisor x-a.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: What symmetry does the graph of cos x have?
addedAccepted: cosine is even, so cos of negative x equals cos of x.
addedRejected: Cosine is odd and cos(-x)=-cos(x).
The cosine graph is reflected into itself across the x-axis rather than the y-axis.

records.subject: Maths
records.front: What symmetry does the graph of sin x have?
addedAccepted: Sine is odd: sin(-x)=-sin(x), giving origin symmetry.
addedRejected: Sine is even and sin(-x)=sin(x).
The graph of sine is symmetric about the vertical y-axis.
